# `Q-5-25` — Alias Paths Differ Only by Case

> Two paths differ only in capitalization, which macOS and Windows
> treat as the same file.

## What this means

Linux filesystems are usually case-sensitive: `Deploy.html` and
`deploy.html` are two files. macOS and Windows, by default, are
not — there, they are one file, and whichever is written second
replaces the first.

This error fires when two `aliases:` entries resolve to paths that
differ only in case, or when one does so against a page the
project renders:

```yaml
# one.qmd
aliases:
  - /Deploy.html

# two.qmd
aliases:
  - /deploy.html      # the same file on macOS and Windows
```

## Why it is checked everywhere

The check runs on **every platform**, including case-sensitive
ones. That is deliberate.

A site built on Linux CI where both files were written looks
correct in the build log. Serve it from a case-insensitive
filesystem — or let a contributor check it out on a Mac — and one
redirect silently disappears. Catching it at build time on every
platform is what makes the output portable.

## How to fix it

Rename one of the two so they differ by more than capitalization.
If both spellings need to work, pick one as the real alias; a
case-insensitive host will serve it for either spelling anyway.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 compares paths as exact strings, so it never notices.
On a case-insensitive filesystem the redirects overwrite each
other silently.
